data: LeanCodeBox is a GitHub organization focused on lean, clean, low-dependency software. We want every project to be cohesive and clearly bounded: easy to understand and deploy, while remaining simple as it evolves.
data.what-we-value#What we value: Keep only the capabilities needed to solve real problems. Organize features and data around clear, cohesive project boundaries. Choose stable dependencies carefully and minimize unnecessary runtimes and external services. Treat deployment, upgrades, documentation, and long-term maintenance as part of the software itself. Current projects include the GooseForum community platform and the Rooster task scheduler.

Welcome to the documentation for LeanCodeBox projects.
GooseForum Deploy and operate a modern community platform Rooster Manage local processes, scheduled tasks, and agent access

GooseForum is a modern community platform built with Go, React 19, and Tailwind CSS. It uses SQLite by default, compiles into a single executable, and works well for independent communities, product support, and technical discussions.
data.capabilities#Capabilities: Markdown topics, replies, categories, and drafts. Notifications, private messages, profiles, and role management. Brand customization and a light/dark theme workbench. SQLite by default, optional MySQL/PostgreSQL, and scheduled SQLite backups. React 19 frontend with GoHTML fallback pages.

data: This document describes the main GooseForum configuration options. On startup, GooseForum checks for config.toml in its working directory and creates a default configuration if the file does not exist.
data.app-application-settings#[app] Applicati: [app] env = "production" # Environment: local, production debug = false # Optional debug override cdn_url = "" # CDN URL env: Controls environment-dependent loading behavior. Use production for production deployments. debug: Optional override. When omitted, debug mode defaults to enabled in local and disabled in other environments. Enabling it provides more detailed log output. cdn_url: CDN URL for static assets.
data.authsession-login-sessions#[authsession]: [authsession] validTime = 604800 # Sliding session lifetime in seconds validTime: Session lifetime; defaults to 604800 seconds (7 days). Active sessions renew when less than one day remains. Existing jwtopt.validTime values remain supported for older configurations. Authentication results are cached in the server process for up to 15 seconds. API logout, revocation, and password changes invalidate that cache. Password changes made by the separate set-user-password CLI process may take up to 15 seconds to invalidate active sessions. Do not run multiple server processes with this local cache.
data.cache-cache-settings#[cache] Cache Setti: [cache] driver = "memory" Only memory is currently supported and is also the default. The backend is validated and frozen at startup; restart after changes. This setting controls sharedcache business read caches. Fixed local caches, login sessions and captcha stores are unaffected. Redis is not implemented; setting redis prevents startup. See cache design .
data.common-problems#Common Problems:
The service does not start
Check whether the port is already in use. Check the configuration file for syntax errors. Read the logs for detailed error messages. The database connection fails
Check whether the database service is running. Verify the connection string. Check the database user’s permissions. Email delivery fails
Check the SMTP settings in the admin console. Verify the mail username and password. Check network connectivity.
data.configuration-file-structure#Configurati:
The configuration uses TOML and contains these main sections:
[app]: Application settings [server]: Server settings [authsession]: Login session lifetime [cache]: Replaceable business cache backend [db]: Database settings [storage]: File storage settings [log]: Logging
data.configuration-reloading#Configuration Re:
GooseForum supports configuration reloading. Changes to config.toml take effect without a restart, except for settings that require one.
Restart the service after changing:
The listening port (server.port) Database connection settings (db.*) Logging settings (log.*)
data.db-database-settings#[db] Database Setti: [db] migration = "on" # Database migrations: on, off backupSqlite = true # Enable scheduled SQLite backups backupDir = "./storage/databasebackup/" # Backup directory keep = 7 # Number of backups to retain spec = "0 3 * * *" # Backup schedule (cron expression) migration: Enables database migrations. Keep it enabled for initial setup and version upgrades. backupSqlite: Enables automatic SQLite backups. backupDir: Directory for backup files. keep: Number of backup files to retain. spec: Cron expression; the default runs backups daily at 03:00.
data.dbdefault-primary-database#[db.default]:
[db.default] connection = "sqlite" # Database type: sqlite, mysql, postgres path = "./storage/database/sqlite.db" # SQLite database path url = "user:pass@tcp(host:3306)/db?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local" # MySQL DSN maxIdleConnections = 3 # Maximum idle connections maxOpenConnections = 5 # Maximum open connections maxLifeSeconds = 300 # Maximum connection lifetime in seconds SQLite example:
[db.default] connection = "sqlite" path = "./storage/database/sqlite.db" MySQL example:
[db.default] connection = "mysql" url = "username:password@tcp(localhost:3306)/gooseforum?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local" maxIdleConnections = 10 maxOpenConnections = 20 maxLifeSeconds = 3600 PostgreSQL example:
[db.default] connection = "postgres" url = "host=localhost port=5432 user=gooseforum password=secret dbname=gooseforum sslmode=disable TimeZone=Asia/Shanghai" maxIdleConnections = 10 maxOpenConnections = 20 maxLifeSeconds = 3600 postgresql is also accepted as the connection name. The url setting may use either PostgreSQL keyword/value format (shown above) or a postgres:// URL.
data.debug-mode#Debug Mode:
To explicitly enable debug mode:
[app] env = "production" debug = true [log] type = "stdout"
data.log-logging#[log] Logging: [log] type = "stdout" # Output: stdout, file path = "./storage/logs/run.log" # Log file path maxage = 10 # Maximum retention in days maxsize = 256 # Maximum file size in MB maxBackUps = 30 # Maximum number of backup log files type: stdout writes to the console; file writes to a file. File logging rotates automatically according to the size and retention settings. maxage: Rotated log files older than this number of days are removed. maxsize: Log files are rotated when they exceed this size. maxBackUps: Number of rotated log files to retain.
data.oauth-login#OAuth Login:
OAuth settings are stored in the database and managed under Settings > OAuth in the admin console. Built-in providers include GitHub, Google, and Discord. You can also add OpenID Connect providers that support Discovery.
The admin console displays the callback URL for each provider. A provider appears on the login and account linking pages only when it is enabled and both its Client ID and Client Secret are configured. Legacy [github] settings are migrated into the database on startup; remove them from config.toml after confirming that migration succeeded.
data.related-documentation#Related Documentat: Quick Start Chinese Configuration Guide Source: GooseForum configuration · 2026-11-15
data.security-recommendations#Security Recomm: Session storage: Protect the database; only SHA-256 hashes of random login tokens are stored there. Database password: Use a strong password and rotate it regularly. Mail password: Use an application-specific password or authorization code. File permissions: Restrict access to the configuration file; mode 600 is recommended. chmod 600 config.toml
data.server-server-settings#[server] Server S: [server] url = "http://localhost" # Base site URL port = 5234 # Listening port readHeaderTimeoutSeconds = 10 # Request header timeout readTimeoutSeconds = 60 # Full request timeout, including upload bodies writeTimeoutSeconds = 60 # Response write timeout idleTimeoutSeconds = 120 # Keep-Alive idle timeout url: Used to generate URLs for features such as RSS and sitemaps. port: The listening port; defaults to 5234. All timeout values are in seconds; 0 disables a timeout. Slow uploads must finish within readTimeoutSeconds.
data.storage-file-storage#[storage] File stor:
Set driver to database or s3. With S3, endpoint is used for server-side I/O and upload signing, while publicUrl is the custom bucket domain or CDN used in public file URLs:
[storage] driver = "s3" [storage.s3] endpoint = "https://s3.example.com" publicUrl = "https://files.example.com" bucket = "gooseforum" accessKey = "your-access-key" secretKey = "your-secret-key" region = "" secure = true pathStyle = false Leave publicUrl empty to keep serving files through GooseForum’s /file/img/ route. A path prefix such as https://cdn.example.com/forum-files is supported. Existing database-backed files are unaffected by the S3 custom domain.
Browser uploads use presigned PUT requests. The bucket CORS policy must allow the site origin to use PUT and the Content-Type request header. GooseForum no longer uses HTML form presigned POST, which Cloudflare R2 does not support.

data:
Run GooseForum as a regular system service and place Caddy or Nginx in front of it for HTTPS and reverse proxying.
Preserve config.toml and the entire storage/ directory. Back up external MySQL/PostgreSQL databases and S3 objects separately if used. For SQLite, use application backups or stop the service before copying the database. Review the target release notes and verify restoration before upgrading.
data.basic-checklist#Basic checklist: Use the production environment. Set server.url to the public HTTPS address. Restrict system permissions for the database and storage directories. Regularly verify that backups can be restored. Forward client IP and protocol headers correctly through the reverse proxy.

data.build-from-source#Build from source:
You need Go 1.27+, Node.js 18+, and pnpm:
git clone https://github.com/leancodebox/GooseForum.git cd GooseForum cd resource && pnpm install && pnpm build && cd .. go build -ldflags="-w -s" . ./GooseForum serve
data.use-a-release-build#Use a release build:
Download the archive for your platform from GitHub Releases :
tar -zxvf GooseForum_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz chmod +x ./GooseForum ./GooseForum serve The server listens on port 5234 by default. The first registered user automatically becomes an administrator.

data: Rooster brings a local web console, native tray app, SQLite execution history, and process management together. Use it for development services, background workers, backups, and synchronization scripts.
data.agent-access#Agent access:
Endpoint Purpose GET /api/health Health check GET /api/skill Agent operating instructions GET /api/docs Complete API fields, responses, and examples The console’s Agent access button copies the current instance address and documentation. An accepted execution request does not mean successful completion; inspect execution history afterward.
The service listens on loopback by default and has no remote authentication layer. Commands execute with the Rooster process user’s permissions. Keep access local.
Source and complete guide · Architecture
data.choose-a-task-type#Choose a task type: Type Use case Behavior Resident resident Development services and background workers Restart on failure, always, or never; exponential backoff Scheduled scheduled Backups, synchronization, checks Five-field Cron; skip overlapping runs or allow parallel execution Run a new task manually, inspect its history and logs, then enable automatic operation. Disabling a scheduled task stops future triggers but does not terminate an active execution. Stop that execution separately if needed. Editing and deletion require a disabled task with no active execution.
data.data-and-environment#Data and environmen: ROOSTER_LISTEN: preferred address, default 127.0.0.1:9090. ROOSTER_DATA_DIR: data directory, default Rooster under the system user configuration directory. The database is rooster.db; logs are in logs/. Preserve the data directory when migrating or backing up. Configure working directories, shells, environment variables, and execution logs per task.
data.quick-start#Quick start:
Install Go 1.25+, Node.js, and pnpm:
git clone https://github.com/leancodebox/rooster.git cd rooster cd web pnpm install pnpm build cd .. go run ./cmd/roosterd Open http://127.0.0.1:9090. If occupied, Rooster tries the next 100 ports; use the address printed in the rooster ready log. The native tray entry is go run ./cmd/rooster and requires the platform’s Fyne graphics dependencies.
